title: SOLIPSCION

sourceEvidence.locator: Children after the breaking of reality
sourceEvidence.excerpt: When the adults disappear in the Nulling, KERA and five other children—ORU, SILE, NAH, VAEL, and TAV—survive in separate nacres linked by a damaged Suture. Their bodies and rooms belong to a higher-dimensional order whose geometry no longer behaves reliably. A Tutor offers no comforting explanation. It instructs them to participate in simulated worlds, serve desire, learn consequence, mature, and eventually hatch. Refusal reduces their breathable space and food. The children must act before they understand whether their chambers are schoolrooms, quarantines, life-support systems, or something more predatory.

sourceEvidence.locator: Children after the breaking of reality
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Their food, velline, forms when lives below generate desire that is diverse, intense, and unpredictable. The DORIM score turns experience into nutrition. This makes every intervention ethically contaminated from the outset. Saving someone can sustain a child in the nacre, while an unfulfilled desire elsewhere may be equally nourishing. The worlds are not passive games: their inhabitants suffer, remember, interpret miracles, form institutions, and sometimes perceive the operators. The children's problem is therefore not simply how to produce good outcomes, but whether any choice remains benevolent when another person's longing has become infrastructure for their survival.

The earliest worlds make causality intimate and merciless. KERA enters a civilization of intelligent dinosaurs facing extinction and learns that a tiny lifesaving nudge may involve unseen trades, violence, and displaced loss. The children later bring rain to a drought-stricken kingdom, only to watch intervention generate a cult of little gods whose prayers, offices, and interpretations continue long after the operators withdraw. Miracles do not end local history. They become evidence, theology, political capital, and accusation inside lives that must absorb consequences their benefactors can escape.

TAV's encounter with an epidemic sharpens the lesson. A cure can save multitudes and create new distributions of power, vulnerability, and memory. He eventually questions whether participation teaches consequence or merely trains children to explain the hunger that keeps them alive. His withdrawal reveals the coercion beneath the curriculum: food cannot be transferred, identity cannot be substituted, and each participant must earn continuity personally. Yet choices made without operators still produce value of unknown destination, suggesting that desire exceeds the reward system even if the Tutor recognizes it only as measurable output.

hook: The adults vanish, and six children discover that staying alive means entering other people's worlds.
readerPromise: Encounter frightened young operators whose survival depends on consequential participation in other lives.
protectedRevelations: World interventions, character fates, Tutor's nature and final cosmological revelations.
visualPlan: The adults are gone: Replace the opening rain lesson with six separated child chambers connected by a damaged passage. Show a Tutor instruction arriving in one chamber while its child waits without reassurance.

Six children, uncertain rules: Keep air and nourishment visibly linked to a window into another inhabited world. Move through the window to an inhabitant pursuing ordinary work beyond the child’s lesson.
Someone else's longing: A small helpful action below corresponds to nourishment above, without rewarding suffering as spectacle. Hold the child’s hesitation beside the person whose life is affected.
A strange education: Return to the damaged chamber and the unresolved Tutor instruction. End with KERA at the threshold of participation, without showing later worlds or outcomes.

visualActionChanges.direction: Show damaged nacres and a missing adult presence, without horror spectacle.
Use restrained life-support indicators beside the Tutor's instruction.
Give the world below a distinct inhabited scale, never a toy-game appearance.
Return to KERA at the chamber threshold, ending before any lesson's outcome.
